facts.fact: The Direction générale des impôts says its e-services portal, launched 23 May 2024 in Cotonou for small businesses and individuals, lets taxpayers declare income online.
The Direction générale des impôts describes the e-services portal as a portal for online declaration and payment (télépaiement) of taxes, with land taxes payable online, since 23 May 2024.
The government says a single online return for payroll tax and social security contributions was launched on 3 February 2020 on the eservices.impots.bj platform.
The government says the single payroll tax and social security contribution return is followed by online payment on the e-services platform, launched 3 February 2020.

note: e-Tax is named as an integrated system; the deck does not say what it does for filing or payment.

facts.fact: Africaho reports that a DGI circular of 16 September 2025 states that payment and affixing of tax stamps and registration of deeds are done exclusively online through the e-services.impots.bj platform, with an electronic stamp carrying a QR code verifiable on the platform.

note: The circular covers tax stamps and deed registration only; online filing of returns is not stated.

facts.fact: ICTD says SIGIBé, which replaced SIGTAS (launched 2018), was rolled out for large and medium taxpayers in 2022 and extended to small businesses in 2024, with the Cotonou centres online since May 2024 and taxpayers able to file online.
ICTD says taxpayers in Benin pay online through SIGIBé, mostly by mobile money, and the DGI reports electronic payments above 96% for most taxes.
